title: Database connection pool exhaustion
steps: Compare active connections with the configured pool size and database connection limit.
Correlate the first error with recent pool-size, worker-count, or connection-lifecycle changes.
Check for leaked connections and long-running transactions before increasing capacity.
Test a conservative pool-size adjustment under representative concurrency.
rollback: Restore the previous pool configuration and restart only the affected worker group.

title: Slow downstream dependency
steps: Compare downstream latency with the caller's request budget.
Check provider status, regional routing, and recent dependency configuration changes.
Verify timeout, retry, and circuit-breaker settings to prevent retry amplification.
Use a bounded timeout and a tested fallback where business semantics permit.
rollback: Restore the previous timeout and circuit-breaker settings.

title: Application/database schema mismatch
symptoms: application expects a schema change not present in database
steps: Compare the deployed application version with the database migration ledger.
Confirm whether the required migration is backward-compatible and safe to run.
Prefer an expand-and-contract migration sequence for production schema changes.
Validate the migration against a production-like snapshot before rollout.
rollback: Roll back the application to the last schema-compatible version; do not drop data-bearing columns.

title: Cache stampede and database read pressure
symptoms: many concurrent misses for the same key
steps: Identify hot keys and determine whether expiration is synchronized.
Check cache eviction, TTL changes, and cache-node health.
Use request coalescing, jittered TTLs, and bounded stale-while-revalidate where safe.
Load-test the cache policy and verify database query rate returns to baseline.
rollback: Restore the previous TTL and disable the new cache-coalescing policy if error rates increase.

title: Memory pressure and worker restarts
steps: Compare heap and resident-set memory across worker restarts.
Capture a heap profile in a safe staging environment.
Inspect caches, retained references, and unbounded queues.
Apply a bounded-cache or lifecycle fix and validate with a soak test.
rollback: Revert the application change and restore the previously validated resource limit.
